content.text: A great smoothie bowl is thick enough to eat with a spoon and topped with enough crunch to make breakfast feel like a treat. The key is using frozen fruit as the base and keeping liquid minimal — typically no more than 1/4 cup.

items: Acai Bowl — frozen acai, banana, mixed berries
Mango Turmeric Bowl — frozen mango, coconut milk, turmeric
Pitaya (Dragon Fruit) Bowl — frozen pitaya, pineapple, coconut water
Green Goddess Bowl — spinach, mango, banana, spirulina
Peanut Butter Chocolate Bowl — banana, cacao, peanut butter, almond milk
Berry Beet Bowl — frozen berries, roasted beet, banana

content.text: For a thick bowl, freeze your bananas the night before and use a high-powered blender. Add liquid one tablespoon at a time until just blended.

Blend one 100g packet frozen acai with 1 frozen banana, a handful of frozen blueberries, and 3 tbsp almond milk until ultra-thick. Pour into a chilled bowl and top with granola, sliced banana, fresh berries, coconut flakes, and a drizzle of honey. Serve immediately.

items.question: How do I keep my smoothie bowl thick?
items.answer: Use mostly frozen fruit, minimal liquid (2–4 tbsp max), and a powerful blender. Chill your bowl in the freezer for 5 minutes before serving to keep it thick longer.

items.question: Are smoothie bowls healthy for weight loss?
items.answer: They can be, but watch toppings like granola, nut butter, and honey which add up quickly. Keep a smoothie bowl under 450 calories by using 1 tbsp of each topping and skipping sweetened granola.
